title: Flyway schema migrations on recon Postgres
subtitle: Expand/contract, freeze windows, abort, and the break_code_v2 example
author: Aman Kumar
audience: SE II and backend engineers shipping recon schema changes; SRE on freeze nights
owners: Aman Kumar (recon schema), Rina Das (DBA), Priya Nair (EM)
related: CLH-TDD-2023-011, CLH-SOP-2023-019, CLH-4419, CLH-4677, CLH-HOTFIX-2024-06-03, ns-pg-clh-recon-01
summary: This SOP is how we change the recon Postgres schema with Flyway without taking down month-end match. Expand, then contract, never in the same release as the code that stops reading the old column. Exclusive locks need Rina Das on the ticket before you merge. The worked example is V142 adding break_code_v2. The failure you will hit at 23:10 is a checksum mismatch after a hotfix that edited a applied file. Commands, freeze windows, and how to abort a migrate that is already running are below.
form_description: Standard operating procedure for Flyway migrations against Clearhaven recon Postgres. Written after the June 3 hotfix checksum incident so expand/contract and abort steps live in one place.
revision_history: Draft the morning after CLH-HOTFIX-2024-06-03 checksum mismatch.
Exclusive lock approval path and freeze window table.
Approved. break_code_v2 example and abort commands from staging rehearsal.

blocks.text: Flyway on recon Postgres

recon Postgres is ns-pg-clh-recon-01 (Postgres 14.10, primary in us-east-1a, sync replica in 1b, async in 1c). Flyway runs from the migrate Job in namespace clearhaven-prod, image ns-clh/flyway-runner:9.22.3, against database clearhaven_recon, schema recon. The history table is recon.flyway_schema_history. We are on version V141 in prod as of 2024-06-17. V142 is break_code_v2, rehearsed in staging, waiting on this SOP to be the written rule rather than tribal memory. If you have never run a migrate here, you still follow this document. The June 3 hotfix proved that editing an already-applied file is worse than being late.

Priya Nair asked me to write this after Flyway refused to start on 2024-06-03 at 23:14 ET because V118's checksum no longer matched. Kavya Menon had patched V118 in a hotfix branch to add a missing NOT NULL on a staging-only column that had somehow been copied into the prod file during a cherry-pick. Prod had already applied the old bytes in January. Flyway's check is doing its job. The outage was 47 minutes of blocked deploys, not a data outage, but it sat on the same night as a RailClear restatement and Helen Cho thought match was down. It was not down. The migrate Job was. This SOP exists so the next person does not edit V118.
Decision (read this first)

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Expand in release N. Dual-write in N. Dual-read in N or N+1. Stop writing the old column in N+1. Drop the old column in N+2 or later, in its own Flyway version, during a freeze window, with Rina Das on the change ticket if the drop takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Never drop a column in the same release as the code that stops using it. Never edit a file Flyway has already applied. Never run Flyway against the primary from a laptop.

Rahul Deshmukh wanted break_code_v2 to ship as one PR: add column, backfill, drop break_code, cut a release. That died in the 2024-06-06 schema review. Dropping in the same release as the code means a failed Helm rollout leaves you with a column the old pods still SELECT and a new file that already dropped it. We have 12 match-engine pods and a rolling update that takes 6.4 minutes. For 6.4 minutes you would have mixed binaries. Mixed binaries plus a dropped column is INC-shaped. Expand/contract is slower by two releases. It is the only shape Rina will approve for recon.leg_break and recon.leg_match_work, which are the two tables that sit on the 7:20 ET path.
What this SOP covers

items: Adding a column, index, or table to clearhaven_recon via Flyway.
Backfills that run inside Flyway versus backfills that must run as a Job because they touch more than 2 million rows.
Freeze windows and who can waive them.
Aborting a migrate that is already executing.
The exclusive lock approval path through Rina Das.
Checksum mismatch after a hotfix, including the V118 incident.
The worked example of break_code_v2 (V142 expand, V143 backfill, V144 contract later).

blocks.text: This SOP does not cover logical replication slot creation, major version upgrades, or partition attachment. Those are Rina's runbooks (NS-DBA-RB-14 and CLH-TDD-2023-011). If your migration ATTACH PARTITION or CREATE INDEX on a table larger than 40M rows without CONCURRENTLY, stop and get her. match-engine's online writes will queue behind your lock and Helen will see unmatched counts climb even though Kafka lag looks fine.
Expand / contract rules

Expand means add the new shape while the old shape still works. For break_code_v2 that is: add column break_code_v2 varchar(32) null, add a check constraint that is NOT VALID, add an index CONCURRENTLY. Application code in the same release writes both break_code and break_code_v2, reads break_code_v2 if not null else break_code. That dual-write is boring and it is required. Kavya's first draft of the match-engine PR wrote only v2. Sneha Iyer caught it in review because a pod on the old binary would read nulls after a partial rollout. Dual-write stayed.

Contract means remove the old shape after every reader and writer has been on the new code for at least one full month-end. For us that is at least 28 days and one 7:20 ET window. Then a Flyway version drops the old column or the old check constraint. That version is its own Helm release. The application chart does not ship code that references the old column in the same release. If you think you can because the Java field is gone and Hibernate will not SELECT it, you are still wrong: on-call debug queries, Grafana, and Helen's Metabase dashboards will SELECT it. Contract is a social process as much as a DDL process. Helen needs a week of notice before break_code disappears from her saved queries.

rows: V143 UPDATE in batches OR a Job, not a single UPDATE
Hours to 2 days, never during 17:00-20:30 ET
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, maybe SET NOT NULL after backfill
Code already ignores break_code for a release
>= 28 days after expand, after one month-end
blocks.caption: Four phases. The June 6 proposal that merged expand and contract into one version is the rejected path.

blocks.text: Never DROP COLUMN in the same release as the code change. If the rollout fails halfway, old pods must still run. If you already merged a drop, revert the Flyway version with a new version that re-adds the column as nullable. Do not flyway undo. We do not enable undo migrations on this database.
What counts as an exclusive lock

Rina Das wants a ticket, a duration estimate, and a rollback sentence for anything that takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on recon.leg_break, recon.leg_match_work, recon.leg_raw, or recon.audit_event. CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY, ALTER TABLE ... SET NOT NULL on a column that does not already have a valid check constraint, DROP COLUMN, ALTER TYPE, and adding a foreign key without NOT VALID all take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on Postgres 14. ADD COLUMN with a volatile DEFAULT also rewrites the table. ADD COLUMN NULL or with a constant default is the cheap one and does not need her, but you still run it in a freeze window if the table is one of the four above.

I asked her on 2024-06-10 whether VALIDATE CONSTRAINT needed the same approval. She said yes if the table is over 40 million rows, because VALIDATE scans, and a scan that fights match-engine autovacuum on month-end is how we got 12-40s write stalls in November 2023 (see CLH-INC-2023-204). recon.leg_break is 91.4 million rows as of 2024-06-17. VALIDATE on that table is a Rina-approved, freeze-window operation. Do not sneak it into a Tuesday afternoon deploy because the PR looks small.
Freeze windows

Rahul publishes freeze windows in #clh-recon-pm. The standing ones are below. A freeze window means no Flyway Job, no manual DDL, no ANALYZE on the four hot tables, unless Priya and Rina both type approve in #clh-prod-changes. Diego can veto if the cluster is already degraded. Helen can veto if unmatched count is over 8,000. Those vetoes have been used. Respect them.

rows: Clearhaven ops morning match, 7:20 SLA clock
Sev-1 data-correctness only, Rina on the call
None needed for ADD COLUMN NULL
blocks.caption: Times are America/New_York. DST is Helen's problem if you schedule a Saturday VALIDATE on the November fallback weekend. Ask her.

blocks.text: The June 3 checksum incident happened at 23:14 on a Monday, outside every window, because the hotfix pipeline runs Flyway on every chart apply. That is a footgun. Diego changed the prod Helm hook on 2024-06-05 so the migrate Job is skipped when the annotation northstar.internal/skip-flyway=true is set on the release. Hotfix charts that do not contain a new V* file must set that annotation. I will reject your hotfix PR if it does not. Kavya's June 3 chart did not contain a new version and still ran Flyway, which is how a checksum mismatch on V118 blocked the hotfix that was trying to ship a log-level change.
Commands (staging first, always)

Staging is ns-pg-clh-recon-stg-01, database clearhaven_recon_stg. It is a subset: 14 days of legs, 6.1 million rows in leg_break, restored from a scrubbed snapshot every Sunday 03:15 ET. If your migration is slow on staging, it is worse on prod. If it locks staging, it locks prod. Do not skip staging because the SQL looks like ADD COLUMN.

# from ops-bastion-03.northstar.internal
# 1. confirm you are not pointed at prod
echo $PGHOST
# expect ns-pg-clh-recon-stg-01.northstar.internal for rehearsal

# 2. dry-run against staging using the same image prod uses
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg delete job flyway-rehearse --ignore-not-found
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: flyway-rehearse
  namespace: clearhaven-stg
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      serviceAccountName: flyway-runner
      containers:
      - name: flyway
        image: 111111111111.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ns-clh/flyway-runner:9.22.3
        args: ["info"]
        envFrom:
        - secretRef: { name: flyway-stg }
EOF
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg logs -f job/flyway-rehearse

# 3. apply on staging
# replace info with migrate. Take a screenshot of the info output first.
# 4. confirm history
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- \
  psql -c "select installed_rank, version, description, checksum, installed_on, success
            from recon.flyway_schema_history order by installed_rank desc limit 8;"
blocks.caption: Staging rehearsal. backoffLimit 0 so a failed migrate does not retry and double-apply a non-transactional CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

blocks.text: Prod migrate

Prod Flyway is a Helm post-install/post-upgrade hook named match-engine-flyway. After 2024-06-05 it respects skip-flyway. The happy path is: merge the SQL into main, wait for the Tuesday 12:40 window, helm upgrade, watch the hook, run the verify queries. You do not kubectl exec flyway on the primary. You do not run flyway from your laptop with a connection string in a shell history. Rina revoked laptop grants for DDL in March after a contractor ran a CREATE INDEX that was not CONCURRENTLY from a cafe. The grant is gone. Do not ask for it back.

# prod info only (read-only role flyway_info)
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- \
  psql "host=ns-pg-clh-recon-01.northstar.internal dbname=clearhaven_recon user=flyway_info" \
  -c "select installed_rank, version, checksum, success, execution_time
       from recon.flyway_schema_history order by installed_rank desc limit 12;"

# what is holding locks right now (run this BEFORE migrate, and during if it hangs)
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
SELECT pid, usename, state, wait_event_type, wait_event,
       now()-query_start AS dur, left(query, 120) AS q
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname = 'clearhaven_recon'
ORDER BY query_start;"

# blocking tree
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
SELECT blocked.pid AS blocked_pid, blocked.query AS blocked_q,
       blocking.pid AS blocking_pid, blocking.query AS blocking_q
FROM pg_stat_activity blocked
JOIN pg_locks bl ON bl.pid = blocked.pid AND NOT bl.granted
JOIN pg_locks kl ON kl.locktype = bl.locktype AND kl.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.relation
                 AND kl.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.page AND kl.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.tuple
                 AND kl.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.virtualxid
                 AND kl.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.transactionid
                 AND kl.pid != bl.pid AND kl.granted
JOIN pg_stat_activity blocking ON blocking.pid = kl.pid;"

# Helm path (from CI, not from a laptop)
helm upgrade match-engine chart/ -f values-prod.yaml --wait --timeout 15m
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod logs -l job-name=match-engine-flyway -f
blocks.caption: Prod info, lock inspection, Helm. If the blocking tree shows match-engine pids, abort. Do not kill match-engine to let Flyway win.

blocks.text: How to abort a migrate that is already running

Flyway 9.22.3 runs each version in a transaction unless the SQL contains CONCURRENTLY or a comment ns:no-tx. If the Job is mid-transaction and you delete the Job, the primary cancels the backend and rolls back. That is the clean abort. If the version is CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, there is no transaction, and killing the backend leaves an INVALID index you must drop before retrying. We rehearsed both on staging on 2024-06-13. Times below are from that rehearsal, not from theory.

items: Decide abort vs wait. If pg_stat_activity shows wait_event lock and match-engine queries are piling up behind it, abort. If it is a sequential scan VALIDATE on Saturday with no blockers, wait.
Announce in #clh-prod-changes: aborting flyway Vxxx, reason, pid.
Capture the pid and the query text. You will need them for the ticket.

If the version is transactional (most ADD COLUMN, most UPDATE batches using a DO block with COMMIT inside are NOT one transaction, careful): kubectl -n clearhaven-prod delete job match-engine-flyway. Then SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid) as flyway_info if the backend is still live 5 seconds later. pg_terminate_backend is Rina-only on this cluster.

If the version is CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY: do not delete the Job first if the index is in the build phase and not blocking writes. CONCURRENTLY is supposed to be friendly. If it is blocking (it can, on a busy table, we saw 7.4 min of increased write latency on staging), cancel, then DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS the invalid name.

Confirm flyway_schema_history. The failed version should have success = false, or not be present if the transaction rolled back. If success = true and the objects are half-there, you are in split-brain DDL. Stop and call Rina. Do not run migrate again.
Fix the SQL, new version number if the failed version recorded success=false (you may repair in place only when Rina says the failed row can be deleted). Never change checksum of a success=true row.

blocks.text:
# abort path we used in the 2024-06-13 staging rehearsal (V142concur on a 6.1M row table)

# 1. find the backend
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
SELECT pid, application_name, now()-xact_start AS xact, wait_event, left(query, 160)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE application_name ILIKE '%flyway%' OR query ILIKE 'CREATE INDEX%';"

# 2. cancel (staging; in prod Rina prefers to be the one who runs terminate)
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "SELECT pg_cancel_backend(84112);"

# 3. delete the Job so Kubernetes does not restart it
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg delete job flyway-rehearse

# 4. if CONCURRENTLY left an invalid index
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
SELECT c.relname, i.indisvalid, i.indisready
FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_index i ON i.indexrelid = c.oid
WHERE c.relname LIKE 'idx_leg_break_code_v2%';"

# 5. drop invalid leftover
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS recon.idx_leg_break_code_v2;"

# 6. history
kubectl -n clearhaven-stg exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
SELECT version, success, checksum, installed_on
FROM recon.flyway_schema_history
WHERE version IN ('142','142.1');"
blocks.caption: Abort rehearsal commands. Prod pids will differ. Do not copy 84112 into prod.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: pg_terminate_backend on the Flyway connection during a transactional ADD COLUMN is fine. pg_terminate_backend during CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY can leave the index INVALID. DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY the leftover before the next migrate or Flyway will error on CREATE INDEX with relation already exists, and then you will be tempted to edit the file. Do not edit the file.
Rina Das approval for exclusive locks

The ticket template is CLH-DBA-LOCK. It is a Jira issue type, not a Slack message. Rina asked for this after two Slack-only approvals vanished when people rotated off. Fill in table, statement, estimated duration from staging, rollback sentence, freeze window you want, and whether match-engine can retry the writes that will queue. Assign to Rina Das. Priya Nair is a watcher. Diego is a watcher if the window is Thursday night. Do not @channel. If she has not commented in one business day, ping once. If the window is tomorrow and she has not commented, slip the window, do not guess.

DROP COLUMN in a later version, not the same one
ACCESS EXCLUSIVE unless a valid check exists (PG14 still conservative)
Do not run without the valid check trick
Drop the NOT NULL in a new version
ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, rewrite-ish depending on PG version; 14.10 still takes the lock
Not rehearsed on prod-sized table yet
ADD COLUMN back, data is gone unless we kept a backup table
Yes if > 2M rows in one session

blocks.text: If Rina is on PTO, the backup approver is Wei Chen (DBA, Oakridge/Riverview alumni, now on the Northstar DBA pool). Wei will not approve DROP COLUMN on recon.leg_break without Rina's written backup. Plan around Rina's calendar. Her PTO the week of 2024-07-01 is already on the freeze calendar. Worked example: adding break_code_v2

break_code today is varchar(16) and stores values like AMT_MISMATCH, QTY_MISMATCH, MISSING_STREET, MISSING_RAIL, UNALLOCATED. Ops and the vendor added reasons that do not fit: PARTIAL_LOT_NEST, TAXLOT_DATE_SKEW, DST_SETTLE_SHIFT, and a pile of vendor-specific codes that Marcus Bell keeps in a spreadsheet. Helen has been stuffing those into recon.break_note, which is a text field, and then searching with ILIKE. That search is 8.2 seconds on a month-end dashboard. Rahul's PRD CLH-PRD-2024-021 (still draft) wants a structured code. We are expanding now so the PRD does not start from a text blob.

V142 (expand): add break_code_v2 varchar(32) NULL, add CHECK (break_code_v2 IS NULL OR break_code_v2 ~ '^[A-Z0-9_]{3,32}$') NOT VALID, no default, no NOT NULL. File: V142__add_break_code_v2.sql. This is the Tuesday 12:40 change for 2024-06-25, pending this SOP. Application PR (match-engine 1.44, break-svc 1.19) dual-writes. Old break_code stays the source of truth for readers that have not deployed. Grafana dashboard 1184 still uses break_code until Helen signs off.

V143 (backfill): we will not UPDATE 91.4 million rows in one statement. The Job ns-clh/break-code-backfill:0.3.1 walks id ranges of 5,000, copies break_code into break_code_v2 where v2 is null, maps the four known overflow strings from break_note via a lookup table recon.break_code_map that V142 also creates. Estimated 4.6 hours on prod if we get 12k rows/s. We got 11.4k rows/s on staging hardware that is smaller, so I am using 8.2k as the planning number for prod, which is 3.1 hours of wall clock plus 40% headroom = 4.3 hours. Saturday 10:00-14:00 on 2024-06-29 is the slot. Rina approved the Job shape, not a Flyway UPDATE, on 2024-06-14. Flyway V143 only creates the map table if V142 did not, and records a sentinel row so we know the Job is allowed to run. The Job is the backfill. Flyway is the gate.

Tighten: after the Job, VALIDATE the check, then a later version SET NOT NULL if and only if a count(*) filter where break_code_v2 is null returns 0 on a quiet minute. I do not know if we will SET NOT NULL in Q3. Nullable v2 with dual-read is enough for the PRD. SET NOT NULL is a lock. We may never do it. That is allowed.

V144 (contract): DROP COLUMN break_code. Not in June. Not in July unless auto-split and the nested RailClear work is quiet. Earliest freeze window I will put on the calendar is 2024-08-17 Saturday, and only if Helen's Metabase collection 22 has been rewritten. Priya has to hear from Helen in writing. If Helen still has ILIKE on break_code, V144 waits.

-- V142__add_break_code_v2.sql
-- expand only. no drop. no not null. no rewrite default.

ALTER TABLE recon.leg_break
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS break_code_v2 varchar(32) NULL;

ALTER TABLE recon.leg_break
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_leg_break_code_v2_shape
  CHECK (break_code_v2 IS NULL OR break_code_v2 ~ '^[A-Z0-9_]{3,32}$')
  NOT VALID;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recon.break_code_map (
  old_code varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  new_code varchar(32) NOT NULL,
  source text NOT NULL,
  mapped_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

INSERT INTO recon.break_code_map (old_code, new_code, source) VALUES
  ('AMT_MISMATCH', 'AMT_MISMATCH', 'legacy'),
  ('QTY_MISMATCH', 'QTY_MISMATCH', 'legacy'),
  ('MISSING_STREET', 'MISSING_STREET', 'legacy'),
  ('MISSING_RAIL', 'MISSING_RAIL', 'legacy'),
  ('UNALLOCATED', 'UNALLOCATED', 'legacy')
ON CONFLICT (old_code) DO NOTHING;

-- index in a separate version if we need CONCURRENTLY outside a tx
-- V142b__idx_break_code_v2.sql with ns:no-tx
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_leg_break_code_v2
--   ON recon.leg_break (break_code_v2)
--   WHERE break_code_v2 IS NOT NULL;
blocks.caption: Expand SQL as it will ship. V142b is a second version because CONCURRENTLY cannot run in the transaction Flyway wraps around V142.

blocks.text: Application dual-write (what reviewers should see)

match-engine 1.44 writes break_code (truncated to 16 chars, same as today) and break_code_v2 (full 32). break-svc 1.19 reads v2 if present else v1. The gRPC OpenBreak path (see CLH-ADR-2024-003, in flight) carries both fields for one release. If your PR drops the old setter, Sneha will fail it. I will fail it. The dual-write test is TestBreakCodeDualWrite in match-engine, and it asserts that a 17-character code is stored whole in v2 and truncated in v1 with a metric break_code_truncated_total. That metric is how we prove Helen's stuffed codes were real. If the metric is zero for two weeks after expand, maybe the 32-char column was optional. I do not believe it will be zero. Marcus's spreadsheet has 41 codes.
Failure: Flyway checksum mismatch after a hotfix

This is the June 3 failure, written so we can execute it without rereading the incident thread. Symptom: the migrate Job fails in 2.1 seconds, Helm upgrade returns non-zero, match-engine pods do not roll, logs show Validate failed: Migration checksum mismatch for migration version 118. Expected checksum -1844229012, but got -992144551. Those numbers are from the incident. Yours will differ. The point is Flyway compared the bytes on disk in the image to the bytes it hashed in January.

What Kavya did: cherry-picked a staging-only ALTER onto V118__leg_break_note_trgm.sql in the hotfix branch because the filename was handy and the staging database had drifted. What the pipeline did: built an image containing the edited V118, ran Flyway on prod, Flyway aborted before applying anything new. What did not happen: data corruption. What did happen: a log-level hotfix sat in the pipeline for 47 minutes while we reconstructed the original V118 from git history, rebuilt, and redeployed. Helen was on the bridge for 20 of those minutes because the Helm failure page looks like a deploy failure, which looks like match is about to bounce.

items: Read the log. Confirm it is checksum mismatch, not a failed SQL statement. If it is failed SQL, that is the abort path above, not this path.
Do not repair_checksum. Do not flyway repair from a laptop. repair is how you paper over a real drift. We do not want drift.

Identify the version. git log --all -- sql/V118*.sql. Restore the file bytes that match prod. The checksum Flyway stored is of the file as applied. git show the commit that was in the image on the applied date (installed_on in flyway_schema_history).
If someone already ran repair in panic, call Rina and Priya. The history table may now match dirty files. That is a different incident.
Build a new image with the restored file plus your actual hotfix (which must not be a change to an applied version). Set skip-flyway=true if you have no new V* file.
helm upgrade. Confirm info shows success=true for the old version and the checksum is back to the expected value.

Open a ticket titled do not edit applied Flyway files, attach the git diff that caused it, assign to the author. Priya wants a name on the diff. This is not a shaming ritual. It is how we found that our cherry-pick docs were wrong.

blocks.text:
# checksum mismatch recovery (read-only until you rebuild)

# 1. what Flyway thinks
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod logs -l job-name=match-engine-flyway --tail=80

# 2. what is stored
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/pg-toolbox -- psql -c "
SELECT version, checksum, installed_on, installed_by, success
FROM recon.flyway_schema_history
WHERE version = '118';"

# 3. restore file from the commit that shipped V118 (example hash from June 3)
git log --follow -- sql/V118__leg_break_note_trgm.sql
git show 7c91e2a4:sql/V118__leg_break_note_trgm.sql > /tmp/V118.orig.sql
# compare to what is in the broken image
# git show HEAD:sql/V118__leg_break_note_trgm.sql

# 4. DO NOT do this unless Rina is on the ticket and the file on disk is already restored
# flyway repair
# We left repair disabled in flyway-runner:9.22.3 by not granting the role permission
# to UPDATE flyway_schema_history. That grant is why June 3 could not be papered over,
# which is what we wanted once we calmed down.

# 5. hotfix chart with skip
helm upgrade match-engine chart/ -f values-prod.yaml \
  --set flyway.skip=true \
  --wait --timeout 15m
blocks.caption: Checksum recovery. The expected checksum from June 3 was -1844229012. Do not paste repair into muscle memory.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Editing an applied migration to 'make staging match' is how you get this failure. If staging drifted, write a new version that is staging-only in the stg folder (we have sql/stg/) or fix staging with a one-off Job that does not live in sql/. Prod sql/ is append-only.
Rejected alternatives

Liquibase. Kavya ran a spike in May because Liquibase's context flags would let us skip V118-style files per environment. It died after Rina compared lock behavior. Liquibase's Postgres support is fine. Our team is not fine. Every runbook, the CI image, and Diego's hook are Flyway. A two-tool shop on one database is how checksum incidents become 'which tool applied V118'. Spike notes are in CLH-SPIKE-2024-05-16. We are not picking it up in FY25.

Squash all migrations into a single baseline each quarter. Rahul liked the cleanliness. I do not. Squash rewrites history and invents a new checksum for work that already ran. The June 3 failure is exactly what a squash would cause on every environment that was one version behind. We baseline only when Rina stands up a new replica from a snapshot and Flyway needs a starting rank. That is a DBA operation, not a quarterly hygiene PR from application engineers.

Run Flyway in GitHub Actions against prod using OIDC. Diego rejected this on 2024-06-12. Actions has no view of pg_stat_activity, cannot see Helen's unmatched count, and would still be running at 17:05 if someone merged at 16:50. The Helm hook at least happens in the same window as the deploy you meant to do. Actions would drift. We keep the Job in-cluster.
Failure modes

rows: Validate failed, Helm non-zero, pods unrolled
Restore file bytes. skip-flyway if no new version. Do not repair.
Abort path. Do not kill match-engine.
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, retry in a new version if the failed version recorded success=false
v2 null on 8% of new rows
You shipped match-engine without the setter. Roll forward, do not drop the column.
Stop the Job. Saturday only. Rina's rule.
Someone SET NOT NULL without VALIDATE
Cancel. Add NOT VALID check, validate later, then not-null if we still care.
Good. Write a new version that adds back what you dropped.
Use the Job. Do not ask Rina for your grant back during an incident.

blocks.text: Verify queries after a successful expand

-- after V142
SELECT attname, attnotnull, pg_get_expr(adbin, adrelid) AS def
FROM pg_attribute a
LEFT JOIN pg_attrdef d ON d.adrelid = a.attrelid AND d.adnum = a.attnum
WHERE attrelid = 'recon.leg_break'::regclass AND attname = 'break_code_v2';

SELECT conname, convalidated, pg_get_constraintdef(oid)
FROM pg_constraint
WHERE conrelid = 'recon.leg_break'::regclass AND conname LIKE '%break_code_v2%';

-- dual-write health, first hour after deploy
SELECT
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE break_code_v2 IS NULL AND created_at > now() - interval '1 hour') AS new_null_v2,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 hour') AS new_rows;

-- should be new_null_v2 = 0 if dual-write is on. If not, the app PR is wrong.

Appendix: what Flyway is allowed to do in one version

items: One expand OR one contract OR one index, not two of those in one file.
ADD COLUMN NULL, CREATE TABLE empty, INSERT into a map table with a known < 100 row list.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in its own version with ns:no-tx.
Comments that do not change bytes after apply. Once applied, comments are frozen too, because they are in the checksum.
Not allowed: UPDATE of a hot table, DROP COLUMN, ALTER TYPE, SET NOT NULL, CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY on a table over 100k rows, GRANT to PUBLIC, anything on pg_catalog.

blocks.text: If you need an UPDATE of 91 million rows, you are writing a Job, not a Flyway version. The Job still needs Rina, a Saturday, and a pause button. The pause button on the backfill Job is SIGTERM, which the 0.3.1 image handles between batches. If your Job ignores SIGTERM, it is not ready for prod. Kavya learned that on a different backfill in 2023 when kubelet evicted the pod and the session kept updating for 11 minutes. Rina still brings it up. Handle SIGTERM.
